turns.text: I'd like to practise a hard parent meeting. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. I'll send END MEETING on its own when I want to stop. I'm Owen's English teacher, and Meredith has just walked into my classroom.
You asked for this meeting. Who decided on Owen's zero?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
You haven't answered me. Who decided, and was Owen heard first?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
11:31 PM. I'm writing that down. Plenty of seventeen-year-olds start late, and you still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
Then turn the screen. And you've dodged my question twice now: was Owen heard before you entered that mark?
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Don't. Was he heard, yes or no?
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.

A kid misquoting Shakespeare isn't a crime, Hale. Show me the page where it appears in Owen's essay. And this is the fourth time you've walked past my question, so I'll ask it once more: did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Save it. Answer me, or we finish this in the principal's office.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final; that's what outlines are for. Put both in front of me. You're laying out exhibits and still refusing the one question I came in with.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

That's a machine's guess, and your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone doesn't establish anything. I have a vendor's guide in my bag saying the same thing. Of everything you've told me, I'd like the version history on paper, in front of me, now.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
There's no off the record, and I'm not here to do your job. Turn the screen.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.
A rewrite for what, when I haven't seen one page of your evidence? Ten minutes. And you still owe me an answer on whether Owen was heard before that zero went in.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? Owen's essay.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.
Go ahead. I'll be in the principal's office before you are, with your own procedure and a written complaint that Owen was never heard.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither. The zero comes off.
